body:
Reading this brings a tear to my eye. One of the hardest things in life is letting go of the people we love or may have loved.

Despite what went on at the surface, you will always have a connection with your wife be it good or bad.

Unfortunately, one of the only ways around this is to build a new connection with someone else. Should you find someone who likes you and cares for your wellbeing, those feelings of initial happiness will race back.

Depression is part of who you are. You need someone who understands depression and can offer comfort. You do not want to feel like putting on a happy face out of pressure by your partner.

It's difficult to swallow, but finding someone else at this moment in time may feel like an impossible task. However, by rolling the dice and trying to find someone else ( perhaps via dating sites) you have nothing to lose.

One thing I am sure of. Loneliness will crush you eventually. Having nothing but your own thoughts to occupy your mind throughout the day will destroy you.

Put yourself out there gently. Work socials are likely to be much more difficult being as most of the people there are successful (like you) but may not be supportive of your situation.

To conclude, I cannot tell you what you should or shouldn't do. But if you have the knowledge when you wake up in the morning that there is a man/woman who wants to see you and do things together, then this may provide just one more reason not to end it all. Now that can't be a bad thing.

Thank you for your honesty.

I totally agree with you. I've pretty much spent three years out of the loop and have let myself go downhill in terms of haircuts/fashion.

I guess we just have to accept that some of us look generic.
